newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Wing Tiek Manila unit projects 1997 net.
newsitem.headline: Wing Tiek Manila unit projects 1997 net.

text.p: The Philippines' National Steel Corp (NSC), the steel manufacturing unit of Malaysia's Wing Tiek Holdings Bhd, forecasts its 1997 net income to more than double to 1.167 billion pesos from the 1996 estimate of 518 million pesos.
In documents released to reporters on Friday, the company said the profits would translate to an earnings per share of 0.50 peso in 1997 from 0.20 peso in 1996.
NSC's revenues are projected to rise by 3.9 percent to 15.872 billion pesos in 1997 from about 15.271 billion pesos this year on the back of a 12 percent growth forecast in steel demand.
The company projects Philippine steel demand to reach 3.682 million tonnes next year from this year's 3.302 million tonnes.
The company also expects to cut down its costs of sales by 7.7 percent to 12.742 billion pesos in 1997 from 13.816 billion.

Wing Tiek on Thursday completed its final payment for the purchase of the Philippine government's shares in NSC in the amount of 3.93 billion pesos, effectively making it the 75 percent-owner of the steel firm.

In a statement, Wing Tiek managing director Joseph Chong said: "Wing Tiek's fulfilment of its financial commitments reaffirm its plans to turn NSC into a major player in the domestic and international steel markets."
Officials also announced NSC will diversify into the construction and shipbuilding businesses.

It will also convert its 274-hectare property in Iligan city, southern Philippines into an economic zone. This project, estimated to cost 616 million pesos, targets to have 80 businesses engaged in steel-related industries.
The company estimates it will be shelling out 289 million pesos for its construction business on equipment and working capital in the first three years of operation.
Its shipbuilding and shiprepair project, which will start in 1997, will have an investment cost of 93.86 million pesos in the first three years.
